title: Public Finance & Fiscal Capacity Atlas
purpose: Model government finance as a system of revenues, spending, assets, liabilities, institutions, contingent obligations and real implementation capacity rather than reducing fiscal condition to one debt ratio.

fiscal_identity.rule: Flows over a period and stocks at a date must remain separate.
core_relations: primary balance − net interest = overall balance, subject to the accounting presentation used
debt stock changes through deficits/surpluses, financing transactions, valuation effects and other stock-flow adjustments
gross debt, net debt and broader public-sector liabilities answer different questions
fiscal_identity.caution: National and international accounting frameworks differ in coverage and consolidation. Every measure must name its definition/source.

balance_sheet_layers.boundary: Valuation and coverage can differ substantially across public accounts.
Contingent liabilities are not the same as current debt; trigger probability and legal terms matter.

fiscal_capacity_vector.question: How broad, stable and administratively collectible is the revenue base?
At what maturities, currencies and costs can government fund itself under normal and stressed conditions?
Can approved spending be converted into delivered services/infrastructure?
How do taxes/transfers respond to economic fluctuations without new legislation?
What room exists for additional borrowing/spending given financing conditions, obligations, institutions and macroeconomic context?
fiscal_capacity_vector.boundary: Fiscal space is context-dependent, not one universal threshold.

fiscal_capacity_vector.question: How are revenues and obligations distributed across central, regional and local governments?
What public assets, enterprises or funds generate services, income or strategic capacity?
How large a shock can be absorbed before major tax, spending, financing or institutional adjustment is required?

analysis_sequence: select stock date and flow period
identify policy commitments and demographic/structural pressures
separate accounting capacity from real productive/administrative capacity

shock_cases.path: higher refinancing costs → interest burden → budget adjustment or additional borrowing
weaker tax base + higher automatic transfers → balance deterioration → financing response
price/support/production effects → household/company support or tax changes → fiscal exposure
financial-system stress → guarantees/liquidity/capital support → contingent liability realization or asset acquisition
population structure → pension/health/labour-base effects over long horizons
capability target → procurement/infrastructure/personnel → multi-year commitments → industrial and fiscal interactions

boundary_rules: Government debt is not household debt; monetary sovereignty, currency, tax authority and institutional setting differ.
A high or low debt ratio alone does not determine sustainability.
Budget authorization is not identical to cash execution or delivered capability.
Project karmic/spiritual debt remains a separate symbolic ledger and must never be merged with public financial liabilities.

worked_cases.title: One country can have two correct debt ratios because the perimeter differs
observations: Eurostat reported Denmark general-government gross debt at 27.9% of GDP at end-2025.
Danmarks Nationalbank reported central-government debt at DKK 235 billion, 7.6% of GDP, at end-2025.
worked_cases.distinction: general government statistical perimeter != central government debt-management perimeter
worked_cases.why_it_matters: A reader who treats both numbers as the same object will think one source is wrong. The correct response is to inspect coverage, consolidation and definition before comparing magnitudes.
next_questions: Is the measure gross or net?
What maturity/interest profile sits behind the stock?

worked_cases.title: A sovereign debt stock is made of instruments with dates and refinancing risk
observations: Danmarks Nationalbank's 2025 debt report describes government financing through bonds and other borrowing, including a 10-year government bond and a two-year USD loan.
The report gives central-government interest costs of DKK 5 billion for 2025.
worked_cases.why_it_matters: Debt sustainability is partly a timing problem. Two governments with the same debt ratio can face different near-term pressure if maturity, currency, rate reset and holder structures differ.

worked_cases.title: An energy shock becomes fiscal only through policy and household/company transmission
worked_cases.observation: EU energy import dependency was 57% in 2024 under Eurostat's definition.
worked_cases.why_it_matters: Energy dependence is not itself public debt. A fiscal effect appears through support choices, tax-base effects, public investment, state-owned enterprise exposure or broader macroeconomic transmission.
